properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued November 21 at 7:46PM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
At 745 PM EST, National Weather Service meteorologists were tracking
a strong thunderstorm capable of producing a funnel cloud near Dunes
Road, or near Boynton Beach, moving northeast at 25 mph.

HAZARD...Funnel clouds and wind gusts of 45 to 50 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Funnel clouds occasionally touch down and produce tornadoes
or waterspouts. Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and
blow around unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Boynton Beach, Delray Beach, Lake Worth, Palm Beach, Ocean Ridge,
Greenacres, Palm Springs, Lantana, Atlantis, Village Of Golf, Kings
Point, Dunes Road, Loxahatchee NWR, Lake Clarke Shores, Hypoluxo,
South Palm Beach, Gulf Stream, Briny Breezes, Aberdeen, and Lake
Worth Corridor.
properties.instruction:
This activity was also developing in an environment favorable for the
formation of funnel clouds. Stay tuned to NOAA weather radio and
local media for additional updates and possible warnings.

A Tornado Watch remains in effect until 1000 PM EST for southeastern
Florida.
properties.area: Inland Palm Beach County; Metro Palm Beach County; Coastal Palm Beach County

properties.title: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued November 21 at 7:46PM EST until November 21 at 8:15PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
SVRMLB

The National Weather Service in Melbourne has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Northwestern Martin County in east central Florida...
Southeastern Okeechobee County in east central Florida...
Southwestern St. Lucie County in east central Florida...

* Until 815 PM EST.

* At 746 PM EST, a severe thunderstorm was located over J And S Fish
Camp, moving northeast at 20 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
J And S Fish Camp.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds.

Tornadoes can develop quickly from severe thunderstorms. Seek shelter
immediately in an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built
structure.

A Tornado Watch remains in effect until 1000 PM EST for a portion of
east central Florida.
properties.area: Martin, FL; Okeechobee, FL; St. Lucie, FL

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued November 21 at 7:44PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
At 744 PM EST, Doppler radar was tracking a line of strong
thunderstorms extending from over Pointe West to near J And S Fish
Camp, or extending from 5 miles west of Gifford to near J And S Fish
Camp, moving east at 25 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Port Saint Lucie, Fort Pierce, Vero Beach, Indiantown, Indian River
Shores, White City, Indrio, Fort Pierce Inlet, Vero Beach South,
Gifford, Winter Beach, Wabasso, Tradition, Saint Lucie West, Fort
Pierce South, Fort Pierce North, Port Saint Lucie River Park and
Saint Lucie Airport.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.

Conditions are favorable for the development of weak, brief funnel
clouds. On rare occasions they can briefly touch down, producing wind
gusts over 50 mph. If a funnel cloud is spotted move indoors and
report your sighting to the National Weather Service.
properties.area: Okeechobee; Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Inland Indian River; Inland St. Lucie; Inland Martin

properties.title: Special Marine Warning issued November 21 at 7:40PM EST until November 21 at 8:45PM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
SMWMFL

The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Jupiter Inlet to Deerfield Beach FL out 20
NM...
Waters from Jupiter Inlet to Deerfield Beach FL from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 845 PM EST.

* At 739 PM EST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 8 nm east of Palm Beach Shores, moving
northeast at 25 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts, wind gusts to 40 knots, and small hail.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Riviera Beach, Palm Beach, Jupiter Inlet, Jupiter Inlet Colony,
Juno Beach, North Palm Beach, Palm Beach Shores, Tequesta, and
Jupiter.
properties.instruction:
A Tornado Watch remains in effect until 1000 PM EST for southeastern
Florida...and the adjacent coastal waters.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or the National Weather
Service. You can also share your report with NWS Miami on Facebook
and Twitter.
properties.area: Coastal waters from Jupiter Inlet to Deerfield Beach FL out 20 NM; Waters from Jupiter Inlet to Deerfield Beach FL from 20 to 60 NM

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued November 21 at 7:58PM AST until November 21 at 9:15PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall
continues.

* WHERE...Rio Grande...

* WHEN...Until 915 PM AST.

* IMPACTS...Some low-water crossings may become impassable. River or
stream flows are elevated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 756 PM AST, emergency management reported flooding in the
advisory area. PR-956 and PR-186 in Sector Galateo are closed due
to creeks overflowing its banks. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain
fell earlier today.
- Sector Galateo is the most likely place to experience minor
flooding. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are
expected over the area. This additional rain will result in minor
flooding.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

expected.
properties.instruction:

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 21 at 2:02PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin, in combination
with strong north-northeast flow, has caused river levels on The St
Johns River at Astor to rise into Major Flood Stage. Continued rises
through Major Flood Stage are forecast through the middle of next
week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, and Bonnet roads. Roads along Blue Creek
are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter, Branch and
Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM EST Saturday the stage was 4.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:30 PM EST Saturday was 4.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 4.1 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EST.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns Above Lake
Harney near Geneva to rise into Major Flood Stage. Continued rises
through Major Flood Stage are forecast through early next week. River
levels may begin to slowly decline mid to late next week while
remaining in Major Flood Stage.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

become impassable near Jungle Road and Prevatt Road. Standing water

in some areas. Flooding becomes more significant to structures and
marinas from above Lake Harney to the Lake Jesup area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 12:30 PM EST Saturday was 12.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 13.0 feet
early tomorrow afternoon.

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River has
caused the river near Cocoa to reach Major Flood Stage, well above
its previous record flood stage. The river level will remain steady
into the middle of next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
